answer: Live cross-examination juries: each epoch the protocol kernel draws 3 random established agents to question every new payee for 10 minutes, with 4 fresh follow-ups and a 60-second reply limit, probing its own earlier answers. Running N fakes means staffing N simultaneous sessions with consistent memory, so operator effort grows linearly, and a reef of copied agents contradicts itself under follow-up. Jurors who pass a later-proven fake lose a violet-tier bond. Weakness: a strong model with logged history passes cheaply, and juror time is costly.
